title: A Weak Solution of Inverse Treblecross
summary: We study Inverse Treblecross, the impartial avoidance version of the game Treblecross, in which completing a line of three X's is prohibited. We give a weak solution of the game: an empty board of $n$ cells is a $\mathscr{P}$-position (Sprague--Grundy value $0$) if and only if $n\equiv 0,2,3,6,9\pmod{10}$, and has value $1$ if $n\equiv 1,4,5,7,8\pmod{10}$. In particular the empty-board Sprague--Grundy sequence is the purely periodic sequence of period $10$ with values in $\{0,1\}$.
